original_extraction.evidence_text:
Pick an activity that’s part of your daily morning routine, such as brushing your teeth, combing
your hair or taking a shower. Totally focus on what you are doing, using all your five senses. For
example, when you’re in the shower notice the different sounds of the water: as it sprays out of the
nozzle, as it hits your body, as it gurgles down the drain. Notice the temperature of the water and
the feel of it in your hair. Notice the sensations of the water running down your back and legs.
Notice the smell of the soap and the shampoo and how they feel against your skin. Notice the visual
patterns of the water on the walls or curtain. Notice the clouds of steam billowing upward. Notice
the movements of your arms as you scrub or shampoo.

---

When thoughts and feelings arise, acknowledge them, let them be and refocus on the shower. As
soon as you realise that your attention has wandered off, thank your mind and refocus on the
shower.

---

For starters, practise connecting with one part of your morning routine each day. Then, as your
ability improves, extend it to other parts.

---

In the next three chapters we’
ll see how connection skills help us deal with painful life experiences.
In the meantime, practise seeing the world through new eyes. And whenever you realise that the
time machine has carried you off, bring yourself back to the here and now.
generation_rules: Select a daily morning routine activity
Focus fully on sensory experiences using all five senses
Acknowledge arising thoughts and feelings without judgment
Thank the mind when attention wanders and refocus on the activity
Gradually extend practice to other parts of the routine
pause_rules: Pause to notice when attention has wandered and to acknowledge thoughts before refocusing on the sensory experience.
original_extraction.psychological_function: Facilitates attention regulation by acknowledging distracting thoughts and gently redirecting focus back to the present sensory experience.
repetition_rules: Practice daily with one part of the morning routine initially, then progressively include more parts as ability improves.

original_extraction.therapeutic_function: Enhances present-moment awareness and mindfulness through focused sensory engagement with routine activities.
